name: Open vs closed weights
summary: Some models' weights can be downloaded and run anywhere; others can only be reached through the provider's service.

text: Some cake recipes are secret: you can only buy the cake at the shop. Others are published so anyone can bake the cake at home.
Closed AI models are like the shop cake. Open-weight models are like the published recipe.
D1.analogy: A secret recipe versus a published one.

text: **Closed models** are used through an API or app. The provider controls updates, safety measures and how data is handled.

**Open-weight models** publish the trained weights. Anyone can download them, run them locally, fine-tune them or inspect them, under the terms of their licence, which ranges from permissive to restrictive.
Open weights aren't the same as open source: the training data and full training code are often not released.

columns.title: Open weights
points: You're responsible for hosting and safeguards

D2.analogy: A secret recipe versus a published one.
D2.analogyBreaks: A published recipe lists every ingredient. Most open-weight models publish the finished weights but not the data or full process, so you can bake the cake but not recreate how the recipe was developed.

predict.question: Which kind of model can you run on your own computer with no internet connection?
options: A closed model reached through an API
predict.explanation: Once downloaded, open weights run on your hardware; closed models live on the provider's servers.

text: Debates: whether releasing powerful weights is safe given that safeguards can be removed, what should count as 'open source AI', and how quickly open models track the closed frontier.
